topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the opening administrative framing and sets out the learning objectives for the lecture.

topics.label: Tumor virology and experimental assays for cellular transformation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the discovery of transforming tumor viruses and cellular transformation assays revealed that cancer originates from the misregulation of endogenous cellular genes.

topics.label: Classification and mechanistic actions of oncogenes and tumor suppressors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the functional definitions of cancer mutations and demonstrate how pathway regulation, allele dosage, and mutant protein behavior determine oncogenic or tumor-suppressive activity.

topics.label: Mechanisms and cellular consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the distinction between sequence and chromosomal instability and examine the specific DNA repair defects, replication errors, and mitotic failures that cause them.

topics.label: Multi-step tumor progression and hereditary cancer predispositions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how the sequential accumulation of genetic lesions drives tumor development and how inherited mutations accelerate this multi-step pathway in clinical syndromes.

topics.label: Conclusion and reading recommendations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding remarks, offers recommended reading, and previews the next lecture.
